subject: Resilience narrative & owner commitments for Q2 QBR
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>, Maria Giraldo <maria.giraldo@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2028-03-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Postmortem recap + preliminary owner list for QBR

Team — sending the concise postmortem and a draft owner roster for the incident on 2028-02-20 that impacted hosted inference in us-west-2 (brief below). I want to get these locked for the Q2 QBR narrative and ensure the exec slides have clear owners and concrete commit dates.

Summary (TL;DR):
- What happened: cache eviction storm + misrouted rolling restart during capacity rebalancing caused 6.3% increase in p95 tail latency for 18 minutes; some requests retried and experienced elevated error rates for a subset of customers (notably Acme Analytics).
- Root cause: combination of an overly-aggressive eviction threshold in the KV cache layer following a model rollout, and an orchestration race that scheduled restarts without traffic-aware draining.
- Impact: partial throughput degradation affecting ~12% of requests in the region, customer-facing errors for 3 customers, and a temporary SLA credit for Acme (preliminary).
- Mitigation in prod: tuned eviction policy, gated restarts with graceful drain hooks, and temporary traffic steering to other regions while we validated fixes.

Attachments: postmortem PDF (attached), SLA heatmap workbook (attached).

Preliminary action items (need owners + due dates for QBR slide):
1) KV cache: implement conservative default eviction + safety guardrails (owner: SRE) — ETA: 2028-04-15
2) Orchestration: add traffic-aware drain + restart gating (owner: infra/orch) — ETA: 2028-04-01
3) Regression tests: add coverage for model rollout eviction patterns (owner: applied-ml infra) — ETA: 2028-04-08
4) Customer remediation: finalize SLA credit calculation for Acme & coordinate comms (owner: account team/ops) — ETA: 2028-03-10

Asks: please confirm or propose alternate owners and commit dates by EOD 2028-03-06 so I can finalize the QBR deck. I'll be at the SRE sync this afternoon to walk through the technical appendix, but leadership framing will come from you, Naomi.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2028-03-04T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Postmortem recap + preliminary owner list for QBR

Thanks, Hannah — this is clear and well-scoped. A couple of leadership notes for the QBR narrative:

- We should present this to the board as a resilience story: what failed, how we detected it, the specific mitigations we implemented in <48 hours, and the longer-term engineering work to prevent recurrence. Avoid deep implementation detail on slide decks — keep that in the appendix.
- I want the customer impact slide to include measured business KPIs for Acme: percent of inference jobs delayed, any SLA credit amount, and whether they opened a support ticket or launched a mitigation on their side. Markus, can you confirm the customer-facing numbers for Acme?
- For exec asks, call out the top-3 owner commitments with measurable deliverables (e.g., 'drain gating tested in canary by X date').

I will fold the final owner table into the QBR slide set if I have confirmations by Monday EOD (2028-03-06). Also, please prepare a short one-pager for the board packet that summarizes the business impact and the mitigation timeline. Vivek — if you have any framing you want emphasized, say now.

Best,
Naomi
VP Product, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2028-03-05T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Postmortem recap + preliminary owner list for QBR

Naomi — quick executive asks to make the QBR slide actionable for the board and for sales/CS reviews:

1) Provide a one-slide "status & next steps" with: risk rating (high/med/low), likelihood of recurrence, near-term mitigations already deployed, top-3 engineering commitments with owners + measurable acceptance criteria, and customer impact in dollar/usage terms (if available).
2) An explicit escalation path if any of the top-3 commitments slip past 25% of timeline — who gets paged, and what's the fallback (e.g., longer-term routing policy).
3) A statement from CS for Acme on whether the customer is satisfied with the remediation and the planned credit. Markus, please capture the CS position in a one-line bullet we can insert.

I've drafted a one-pager that frames the incident as a learning and shows where we are on the L1/L2 fixes. Attaching it — please reference the "resilience-one-pager-for-execs.pdf" in the Drive folder.

-Vivek
Chief Revenue & Ops Officer

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>, Maria Giraldo <maria.giraldo@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2028-03-05T15:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Postmortem recap + preliminary owner list for QBR

Folks — confirmed customer metrics and owner commitments below. I pulled numbers from the incident telemetry and CS notes.

Customer impact (Acme Analytics):
- % of inference requests affected (region us-west-2): 6.3% p95 tail influence, ~0.8% total error rate increase across their account during the 18-minute window.
- Business effect: ~2,400 delayed jobs, estimated incremental cost/impact $1,700 (preliminary; finance review pending).
- CS position: CS lead (Maria Giraldo) confirmed Acme is accepting the proposed SLA credit and wants a short technical write-up for their ops team.

Owner commitments for QBR slide (finalized):
1) KV cache guardrails — Owner: Hannah Schmitt (SRE). Deliverable: conservative defaults in runtime + unit tests; Canary validation completed by 2028-04-10.
2) Orchestration drain gating — Owner: Markus Klein (Infra). Deliverable: traffic-aware drain implemented and validated in canary; rollout to prod by 2028-04-03.
3) Model rollout regression tests — Owner: Rishi Malhotra (Applied ML) [cc'd proactively to coordinate]. Deliverable: test suite added to release pipeline; ETA 2028-04-08.
4) Customer remediation & comms — Owner: Naomi Feldman (Product) with CS/Accounts. Deliverable: SLA credit issued and customer technical write-up delivered by 2028-03-10.

I've uploaded a small spreadsheet with the telemetry slice and a short extract to the Drive link Naomi referenced. Attachments: sla-heatmap-q2.xlsx (telemetry slice) and the postmortem PDF.

-Markus
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Thanks, all — this is exactly what we need. Final confirmations accepted; I'll incorporate the owner table and the one-pager into the QBR deck. Specific next steps for us:

- Markus: please ensure the drain gating PR is ready for review by 2028-03-20 so we can hit the canary validation ETA.
- Naomi (me): I'll own the customer comms and SLA credit coordination with Maria; Maria, expect a draft credit calculation from me tomorrow.

I'll schedule a 30-minute QBR prep slot on 2028-03-08 14:00 PT to review the slide and the one-pager; invite will follow. If anything changes on owner timelines, escalate to me and Vivek immediately.
